question: Using an integrating factor, solve $$\frac{dy}{dx}+y\tan x=\sin x$$ on an interval where $\cos x\neq0$.
explanation:
Step 1: Identify $P$ and $Q$
The given equation is in the linear form $$\frac{dy}{dx}+P(x)y=Q(x),$$ with $P(x)=\tan x$ and $Q(x)=\sin x$.
Step 2: Calculate the integrating factor
$$\text{I.F.}=e^{\int\tan x\,dx}=e^{\log|\sec x|}.$$ On the chosen interval, an integrating factor may be taken as $\sec x$.
Step 3: Multiply the equation by the integrating factor
$$\sec x\frac{dy}{dx}+y\sec x\tan x=\tan x.$$ Hence, $$\frac{d}{dx}(y\sec x)=\tan x.$$
Step 4: Integrate
Integrating both sides gives $$y\sec x=\int\tan x\,dx+C=\log|\sec x|+C.$$
Step 5: Express $y$ explicitly
Therefore, the general solution is $$\boxed{y=\cos x\left[\log|\sec x|+C\right]}.$$
